Method of Attack: Encrypts files and appends extensions (e.g., .Exte for CryptoMix, .Scorpio for Scorpio, .OXR for Oxar, .locked for Bit Paymer and Keep Calm, .Malki for AslaHora, .dcry for Dcry, .purge for Purge, .Ransed for Ransed, .kill for Jigsaw, .country82000 for SamSam)
Locks device and threatens to send user's private data to contacts (LeakerLocker)
Drops ransom notes with specific names (e.g., IF_YOU_WANT_TO_GET_ALL_YOUR_FILES_BACK_PLEASE_READ_THIS.TXT for Scorpio, .readme_txt for Bit Paymer)
Uses hardcoded MySQL credentials to connect to server (Ransed)
Screenlocker with spelling and grammar errors, can be closed with Alt+F4 (Unnamed screenlocker)
In-development ransomware with lock screen but no encryption (BrainLag)
Fake screenlocker with passcode A01B (Fake ENDcrypt0r)
Impacted Systems: Files encrypted with various extensions as noted
Indicators of Compromise: Hardcoded MySQL credentials in Ransed ransomware
